title: China publishes 12-point position paper on the Ukraine crisis
body:
On 24 February 2023, the first anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion, China published a 12-point position paper on the political settlement of the Ukraine crisis. Commentators described it as largely a restatement of existing Chinese positions rather than a detailed peace plan.

The first point calls for upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries. The paper urges Russia and Ukraine to resume peace talks, saying that "dialogue and negotiation are the only viable solution". It discourages the threat and use of nuclear weapons, opposes chemical and biological weapons, and urges both sides to follow international humanitarian law and avoid attacking civilians. It criticises what it calls "Cold War mentality" and the expansion of military blocs, widely read as a reference to NATO, and says unilateral Western sanctions on Russia create new problems. The paper also backs the Black Sea Grain Initiative and calls for stable industrial and supply chains.

Reactions were sceptical. U.S. national security adviser Jake Sullivan said his first reaction was that the paper "could stop at point one". Jorge Toledo, the EU ambassador to China, said that Beijing has "a special responsibility" to uphold UN goals and that it was unclear whether the paper was compatible with neutrality. A Ukrainian embassy representative in China said that a neutral China "should talk to both sides".
